US FACTORY ORDERS SURGE 1.8%, BEATING EXPECTATIONS US factory orders rose 1.8% in September, exceeding the 1.2% consensus forecast and accelerating from August's upwardly revised 0.3% gain. Orders excluding transportation increased 1.3%, while orders excluding defense jumped 2.0%, signaling broad-based manufacturing strength. Durable goods orders were revised higher to +1.9%, and core capital goods orders improved to +0.6%, with shipments rising 1.2%.

US JOB OPENINGS RISE TO 7.52 MILLION IN SEPTEMBER US job openings increased to 7.523 million in September, up from an upwardly revised 7.190 million in August, signaling stronger labor demand. Hiring rose to 5.402 million, while voluntary quits climbed to 3.365 million, pushing the quits rate to 2.1% from 1.9%. Meanwhile, layoffs declined to 1.641 million from 1.768 million, with the layoff rate falling to 1.0%.
